title: Adjective Declension 5: Instrumental Singular
description: The instrumental singular for hard-stem adjectives. Masculine and neuter share -ым (with husher / velar -им). Feminine reuses -ой. Triggers: с + accompaniment, instrumental of profession (работать кем), means of transport, the prepositions с / за / под / над / перед.
descriptionRussian: Творительный падеж единственного числа: мужской и средний делят -ым (с правилом для шипящих и заднеязычных, дающим -им), женский повторяет -ой.
intro: The feminine has now held the same form for three cases running, which is the biggest single saving in this book. The masculine and neuter take one more new ending, and this is where the velar and husher spelling rule starts firing on adjective endings again. Same rule as always, applied to a new slot.
rules: Masculine and neuter share one instrumental singular ending: -ым. Hard-stem -ый and -ое both become -ым.
Spelling rule (Rule 1): after к, г, х, ж, ш, ч, щ, write -им not -ым. Маленький → маленьким; хороший → хорошим; русский → русским. Same rule applied in the A1 adjective track's plural -ие.
Feminine takes -ой in the instrumental, the same form as the genitive and dative. Three cases converge on -ой for the feminine slot.

Triggers: с + instr (accompaniment), bare instr for profession (работать кем), bare instr for tools, prepositions за / под / над / перед + instr (static location), reflexive verbs (гордиться, интересоваться, пользоваться, заниматься) + bare instr.
examples: Маша пьёт чай с новым другом. (Masha drinks tea with the new friend.) С + instr; друг masc: новым.
Антон стал хорошим инженером. (Anton became a good engineer.) Profession in past / future / стать; husher rule: хороший → хорошим.
Маша гордится умной сестрой. (Masha is proud of her smart sister.) Гордиться + instr; сестра fem: умной.
Книга лежит под маленьким столом. (The book is under the small table.) Под + instr (static location); velar rule: маленький → маленьким.
Лена пишет новой ручкой. (Lena writes with a new pen.) Bare instr for tools; ручка fem: новой.
Антон занимается русским языком. (Anton studies the Russian language.) Заниматься + instr; husher / velar rule: русский → русским.

items.hint: Recap from Lesson 4: помогать takes which case? Друг is masc.
items.explanation: Recap from Lesson 4. Помогать + dat. Друг is masculine, so the dative ending is -ому: старому. Today's drill, starting Q1.2, switches to the instrumental.

items.promptEnglish: Masha drinks tea with the new brother.
items.hint: С + instr. Брат is masculine. The masculine instr ending is brand new today.
items.explanation: С + instr triggers the instrumental. Брат is masculine, so the instr ending is -ым: новым. Notice both the noun and the adjective shift in parallel: брат → братом (noun -ом), новый → новым (adj -ым).

items.hint: Стал + instr for profession. Хороший stem ends in -ш: which Rule 1 form is correct?
items.explanation: 'Стать + instr' marks the new profession. Инженер is masculine. Хороший ends in -ш-, so by Rule 1 (never write -ы after ш) the instrumental is хорошим, not хорошым. The same -им would appear with русский (русским) and маленький (маленьким).

items.promptEnglish: Masha is proud of her smart sister.
items.hint: Гордиться + instr. Сестра is fem. The feminine instr ending is the same as which other case?
items.explanation: Гордиться + instr. Сестра is feminine, so the instr ending is -ой: умной. -ой is the same form as the genitive (Lesson 3) and the dative (Lesson 4). Three cases converge on the feminine -ой; the trigger decides which case is at work.

items.promptEnglish: The book is under the small table.
items.hint: Под + instr (static location). Маленький stem ends in -к-: which Rule 1 form?
items.explanation: Под + instr marks static location. Стол is masculine. Маленький ends in -к-, so by Rule 1 (never write -ы after к) the instr ending is -им not -ым: маленьким. The same -им appears in русским, хорошим, большим.

items.hint: Заниматься + instr. Язык is masc. Русский stem ends in -к-: which Rule 1 form?
items.explanation: Заниматься + instr (a reflexive verb that takes a bare instrumental). Язык is masculine. Русский ends in -к-, so by Rule 1 the instr is русским. Pattern check: by the end of this lesson маленьким, хорошим, русским should feel like one family with one rule.

blanks: Лена пишет _____ ручкой. (Lena writes with a new pen.)
fillInBlank.grammarFocus: Bare instrumental marks the tool. Ручка is feminine, so the adjective ending is -ой: новой. Both the noun and the adjective end in -ой here, but that is coincidence: ручка → ручкой (noun -ой), новая → новой (adj -ой).

minimalPairs.contextEnglish: Masha drinks tea with the new friend.
minimalPairs.explanation: С + instr triggers the instrumental, not the dative. The masculine instr ending is -ым: новым. Новому would be the dative ('я помогаю новому другу').

minimalPairs.contextEnglish: The book is under the small table.
minimalPairs.explanation: Под + instr triggers the instrumental, not the dative. The masculine instr ending after -к- is -им: маленьким. Маленькому would be the dative form ('я иду к маленькому брату').

errorCorrection.sentence: Мы живём рядом с большым парком.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: We live next to a big park.
errorCorrection.explanation: After -ш-, Rule 1 forbids -ы, so the instrumental is spelled -им: большим. Большым is the mechanical -ым form that the spelling rule blocks; it is not a valid Russian spelling.

errorCorrection.translationEnglish: Masha is proud of her interesting work.
errorCorrection.explanation: Гордиться takes a bare instrumental, and the feminine instrumental ending is -ой: интересной. Интересному is the masculine/neuter DATIVE, a slip if you misread the case; the dative would be right only after a dative trigger like помогать.

After -к-, Rule 1 forbids -ы, so the instrumental is spelled -им: английским. Английскым is the mechanical -ым form the spelling rule blocks and is not valid. The plain -ым spelling appears only after other consonants (новым).

errorCorrection.translationEnglish: The book is under the tall table.
errorCorrection.explanation: Под answering 'where' takes the instrumental for static location, and after -к- the adjective takes -им: высоким. Высоком is the PREPOSITIONAL form (о высоком столе), a natural confusion because both cases handle location questions.

errorCorrection.sentence: Маша пьёт кофе со старый другом.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: Masha drinks coffee with her old friend.
errorCorrection.explanation: С meaning 'together with' triggers the instrumental, so the masculine adjective takes -ым: старым. Старый is the nominative, correct when the friend is the subject (Старый друг пришёл).

A profession after стать takes the bare instrumental, and the feminine instrumental ending is -ой: известной. Известная is the nominative, correct when she is the subject (Известная учительница вошла в класс). The instrumental of profession answers 'became what / works as what'.

errorCorrection.translationEnglish: Right now Masha is busy with an interesting project.
errorCorrection.explanation: Заниматься takes a bare instrumental, and the neuter shares the masculine instrumental ending -ым: интересным делом. Интересное is the nominative/accusative neuter form, correct when дело is the subject or direct object.

reviewVocab.definition: instrumental case (marks the instrument, means, accompaniment, profession; answers 'Кем? / Чем?')
reviewVocab.example: В предложении 'Маша гордится умной сестрой' слова 'умной' и 'сестрой' стоят в творительном падеже.

reviewVocab.definition: profession (the bare instrumental marks the role one plays after the verbs работать, стать, быть in past or future tense)
reviewVocab.example: В предложении 'Антон стал хорошим инженером' слова 'хорошим' и 'инженером' обозначают профессию.

reviewVocab.definition: to be proud of (takes a bare instrumental: гордиться кем / чем)
reviewVocab.example: Маша гордится новой школой и умной сестрой.
